instructions: Operational service knowledge for this repository. Call knowledge_evidence_for_files before reading service source, and knowledge_search before grep, whenever the symptom-to-service mapping is unclear. Call knowledge_status when results look stale or empty, and knowledge_drift before trusting knowledge about recently changed code. These tools return evidence with citations, never conclusions.

tools.name: knowledge_search
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Search this repo's operational service knowledge (architecture, failure modes, runbooks, probes). Call it before grep when the symptom-to-service mapping is unclear. Read-only; returns evidence, never conclusions.
PARAMETERS: query (string, required): symptom, alert, metric or concept. service_id (string): restrict or boost one service. paths (string[]): file paths for territory routing. limit (integer 1-7, default 7): maximum items. consumer_root (string, optional): repo root to read; must be the session root or one of its ancestors, default: the session root.
RETURNS: An evidence bundle: routing, items (id, service_id, title, section_path, text, score, signals, status, risk, section_sync_ref, section_date, superseded_candidate), citations, verification, probes, skill_links, truncated and totals, consumer_root_resolution. Items, citations, probes and item text are trimmed to fit about 8000 tokens (conflicts_and_caveats is never trimmed): truncated=true means something was cut, and totals holds the counts before trimming (items counted after the 7-item cap).
EMPTY OR STALE: items=[] means nothing in this checkout's index matched; it is not proof the knowledge base has no answer, so read consumer_root_resolution first: stale=true means a newer primary checkout exists (retry with the consumer_root in its hint). superseded_candidate=true means a newer sync section of the same service exists, so this section may be superseded: check the newer section. stale_served=true means the index could not be refreshed within its time budget and an older cache was served because the refresh exceeded its time budget or failed; routing.freshness_notice says so.
EXAMPLE: {"query": "bar backfill swap", "service_id": "ingest", "limit": 5}

query.description: Free-text query (alert name, metric, concept, path).

service_id.description: Restrict/boost to a specific service id.

tools.name: knowledge_get
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Fetch one knowledge item by id, or one full SKILL.md by path, when a search hit needs its full text. Read-only.
PARAMETERS: item_id (string): stable item id from a search hit, for example 'section:alertmanager:failure-modes'. skill_path (string): repo-relative SKILL.md path. Pass exactly one of the two. consumer_root (string, optional): repo root to read; must be the session root or one of its ancestors, default: the session root.
RETURNS: {item: {...}} with full text, citations and a link to its skill, or {skill: {...}} with the whole SKILL.md, plus consumer_root_resolution. Errors come back as {error: message} alone; there is no consumer_root_resolution field on an error.
EMPTY OR STALE: 'item not found' or 'skill not found' means the id or path is not in this checkout's index: search again for a current id. When this checkout is a worktree behind the primary checkout, the error message ends with a bracketed hint naming the consumer_root to retry with.
EXAMPLE: {"item_id": "section:alertmanager:failure-modes"}

skill_path.description: Repo-relative SKILL.md path for the full skill.

tools.name: knowledge_evidence_for_files
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Find the service knowledge that owns a set of files, before reading their source. Routes by service territory ownership. Read-only.
PARAMETERS: paths (string[], required): repo-relative file paths. limit (integer 1-7, default 7): maximum items. consumer_root (string, optional): repo root to read; must be the session root or one of its ancestors, default: the session root.
RETURNS: An evidence bundle: routing, items (with section_sync_ref, section_date, superseded_candidate), citations, verification, probes, skill_links, truncated and totals, consumer_root_resolution. Items, citations, probes and item text are trimmed to fit about 8000 tokens (conflicts_and_caveats is never trimmed), so a service with many citations returns the first ones: truncated=true and totals give the counts before trimming (items counted after the 7-item cap).
EMPTY OR STALE: items=[] means no registered service territory covers these paths, or this checkout's index is older than the primary checkout: read consumer_root_resolution.stale before treating the files as unowned. superseded_candidate=true marks a section older than the newest sync section of that service; it may be superseded, so check the newer one.
EXAMPLE: {"paths": ["src/market_data/backfill/swap.py"], "limit": 3}

paths.description: File paths to build evidence for.

tools.name: knowledge_status
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Check whether this repo's service knowledge is installed, indexed and current, and which versions are involved. Call it when results look empty or stale. Read-only; never writes or rebuilds.
PARAMETERS: consumer_root (string, optional): repo root to inspect; must be the session root or one of its ancestors, default: the session root.
RETURNS: consumer_root, registry_present, packs (name, umbrella, services), service_count, index_present, git_head, services_out_of_sync, usable, cli_version (the installed command), pack_version (the machinery vendored in this repo, null when absent), version_mismatch (true, false, or null when pack_version is absent) with version_note, plus consumer_root_resolution.
EMPTY OR STALE: registry_present=false means this repo has not adopted service-knowledge: the retrieval tools (knowledge_search, knowledge_get, knowledge_evidence_for_files) refuse here. version_mismatch=true means the repo's vendored machinery and the CLI differ; version_note says which side is older and what to do (`service-knowledge update` only when the repo is the older side). services_out_of_sync lists services whose last_sync_ref differs from git_head. consumer_root_resolution.stale=true means the primary checkout is ahead of this worktree.
EXAMPLE: {}

tools.name: knowledge_drift
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Report which services' knowledge has drifted from the code they describe. Call it before trusting knowledge about recently changed code. Advisory; never blocks work. Read-only.
PARAMETERS: consumer_root (string, optional): repo root to inspect; must be the session root or one of its ancestors, default: the session root.
RETURNS: git_head, marker_present and marker (reason, services, commit range, timestamp), service_count, services_behind_head (service_id, last_sync_ref), services_never_synced, drift_detected, suggested_action, plus consumer_root_resolution.
EMPTY OR STALE: drift_detected=false with empty lists means every service's last_sync_ref equals git_head and no drift marker is pending. services_never_synced lists services with no last_sync_ref: their knowledge has no verified baseline. Drift is judged against this checkout's HEAD, so check consumer_root_resolution.stale in a worktree.
EXAMPLE: {}
